From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, Niklas Sørensen <niklas@opsly.io>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-12T13:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on June 29 / INV-2048 — telemetry findings

Niklas / Ben — I pulled the telemetry for opsly-prod-305 for the requested window and attached a short snippet (sample-telemetry-snippet.txt). Summary of findings:

- We observed a burst from 2026-06-29T02:07:14Z to 2026-06-29T03:59:48Z where token counts per request jumped ~4.8x relative to baseline.
- Many requests during the burst had identical payloads but different request IDs / idempotency keys. The KV cache shows separate sessions created for those requests, which led to duplicate decoding work and repeated token charging.
- Trace IDs (Redwood) that correlate to your supplied IDs: rwd-20260629-7a1b, rwd-20260629-7a1c, rwd-20260629-7a1d (see snippet).

Initial root-cause hypothesis: client-side retries with mutated idempotency keys (likely due to the load balancer or client-side retry wrapper) caused the same logical calls to be treated as distinct by our runtime. This produced duplicate billing work. We do not see evidence of server-side replays from our routing layer.

Recommended immediate mitigations:
- We can apply a one-time invoice adjustment for the duplicate work once billing confirms the scope.
- Opsly can add a stable idempotency key at the client or use the request-signature header we provide. We'll share a short integration note if helpful.

Attaching: sample-telemetry-snippet.txt (contains trace id mapping and token deltas). Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to go through traces live.

Marissa Cole
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: sample-telemetry-snippet.txt
